references.text: Refers to the consequences of eating from the tree, which led to humanity's fall
God explains the consequences of Adam's action, including death as a direct result of his disobedience
Connects Adam's sin with the death that came upon all people
Reinforces the idea that Adam's disobedience brought sin and death to many
Links the death that came through one man (Adam) with the resurrection that came through Christ
'The soul who sins shall die' – directly links sin to death, which is the core principle of God's warning
Confirms that death is an inevitable part of human existence as a result of sin
Describes how desire leads to sin and sin leads to death – expanding on the principle in God's warning
Presents the choice between life and death, reflecting the fundamental choice in God's command to Adam
The verses show the connection between God's original command and humanity's distorted version of it in the fall, illustrating how sin enters through a change in God's word.
